issue.title: MacBook chezmoi apply fails in install_nvim because cmake is missing
issue.description:
Discovered by epic phase bob-cli-1n.5 (Provision credentials, triggers, and the MacBook git clone) while shipping the chezmoi rsync bridge and Bob config to the MacBook. Recorded there as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1.

A broad `/opt/homebrew/bin/chezmoi apply` on the MacBook fails inside `.chezmoiscripts/install_nvim` because `cmake` is not installed. The phase worked around it by running targeted `chezmoi apply --include files` invocations instead of a full apply, which was enough to land that phase's files but leaves the MacBook unable to take a plain `chezmoi apply`.

That workaround is a trap for every later agent and for the user: the obvious command fails, and the non-obvious `--include files` form is recorded only in a phase-bead note on a now-closed epic. Anyone shipping a future dotfile or script change to the MacBook hits the same wall.

The chezmoi dotfiles live in the `chezmoi` linked repo (see the athena project's CLAUDE.md); open it with `/sase_repo` before editing. Filed against bob-cli because that is where the epic that discovered it lives, matching the precedent set by bob-cli-1h.

Proposed by bob-cli-1n.5, filed by bob-cli-1n.land.

task_type_fields.impact: Blocks any plain `chezmoi apply` on the MacBook, so every dotfile or managed-script change to that machine needs a non-obvious targeted invocation that is documented only in a closed epic's phase-bead note. Epic bob-cli-1n now ships the xlib rsync bridge (`bob_xlib_pull`), the Bob config, and the vault-sync LaunchAgent through chezmoi, so the MacBook depends on chezmoi apply working for future sync-channel maintenance. The install_nvim script also declares a Neovim build prerequisite the machine does not satisfy, so the MacBook's managed Neovim is not being installed or updated.
task_type_fields.location: .chezmoiscripts/install_nvim in the chezmoi linked repo, as applied on kellys-macbook-pro
task_type_fields.repro: On the MacBook, run a broad apply: `ssh mac '/opt/homebrew/bin/chezmoi apply'`. It fails in .chezmoiscripts/install_nvim because cmake is absent from the machine. Narrowing to `chezmoi apply --include files` succeeds, which is the workaround epic phase bob-cli-1n.5 had to use to ship the vault-sync bridge and Bob config.
